newsitem.title: USA: US court acts on Sallie Mae loan case.
newsitem.headline: US court acts on Sallie Mae loan case.

text.p: A U.S. court Friday struck down a 1991 decision that applies a 30 basis point fee to any loan in which the Student Loan Marketing Association holds an interest, Sallie Mae said.
But the Court of Appeals here also remanded the case to a District court with instructions to remand the matter back to the Secretary of Education.
It is uncertain what the ultimate resolution of the issue will be, Sallie Mae said in a statement.
The court's action struck down a 1991 interpretation by the Secretary of Education that the fee -- contained in the 1993 budget act -- applied to all Sallie Mae loans, including securitized assets.
Sallie Mae filed a suit in April saying the fee should not apply to securitized assets, which Sallie Mae does not own.
